# brig up

Make a VM ready to work in, and list its sandboxes

## Synopsis

```text
brig up [NAME] [--create [-- CREATE-FLAGS...]]
```

## Description

Start the VM if it is stopped, or reconnect it if it runs, wait until its
gateway answers and apply its OpenShell config directories, as [`brig start`](brig-start.md)
--wait does. Then list its sandboxes and the drafted network rules that wait
for your review.

With --create, a VM that does not exist is created first, with the flags of
[`brig create`](brig-create.md) that follow --; they do not change a VM that exists. brig up is
therefore safe to repeat, which scripts and the start of a day want.

It fails with exit status 3 if the VM does not exist and --create is not
given, 5 if the gateway does not answer and 6 if the sync fails.

## Examples

```sh
brig up dev
brig up dev --create -- --memory 16GiB --mount ~/src:/mnt/src:sandbox
brig up -o json
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--create` | create the VM if it does not exist, with the brig create flags after -- |
| `-o, --output format` | output format: table or json (default `table`) |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
